sources.author: Kuikanmäki, Jari, and Matti Virtanen
sources.title: Did the Wuhan Virus Institute Trigger the Coronavirus Pandemic? – More Evidence for the Laboratory Theory
sources.summary: Author’s archived AlfaTV piece arguing accumulating evidence that WIV may have triggered the pandemic—Finnish-language lab-theory roundup.

sources.title: Understanding the Risk of Bat Coronavirus Emergence (including the Year-5 Interim RPPR)
sources.summary: NIH FOIA release of EcoHealth bat-coronavirus emergence materials including the late Year-5 interim RPPR describing WIV experiments.

sources.author: Tabak, Lawrence
sources.title: Letter to Rep. Cathy McMorris Rodgers (House Committee on Energy and Commerce), regarding EcoHealth Alliance grant materials
sources.publication: National Institutes of Health, Department of Health and Human Services
sources.summary: NIH Principal Deputy Director Lawrence Tabak’s letter to Rep. McMorris Rodgers transmitting EcoHealth grant materials and acknowledging limited experiments that should have triggered further review.

orgs: U.S. House Energy and Commerce Committee

sources.author: Eban, Katherine
sources.title: In Major Shift, NIH Admits Funding Risky Virus Research in Wuhan
sources.summary: Vanity Fair on NIH’s major shift admitting it funded risky virus research in Wuhan via EcoHealth—coverage of the Tabak letter fallout.

sources.author: Mallapaty, Smriti
sources.title: Closest known relatives of virus behind COVID-19 found in Laos
sources.summary: Nature news on BANAL bat coronaviruses from Laos—closer relatives to SARS-CoV-2 than RaTG13 in key spike regions—complicating simple Wuhan-only stories.
sources.book_role: BANAL-52 discovery showing close sarbecovirus relatives in Laos, still not a direct progenitor.

sources.author: Demaneuf, Gilles
sources.title: Overview of Biological Laboratories in Wuhan and their roles in Coronavirus Research
sources.summary: Demaneuf overview mapping Wuhan’s biological laboratories and their coronavirus-research roles—beyond WIV alone.

sources.author: Pekar, Jonathan, et al.
sources.title: Timing the SARS-CoV-2 index case in Hubei province
sources.summary: Science paper timing the SARS-CoV-2 index case in Hubei—molecular-clock estimates of when the outbreak began relative to reported December cases.

sources.author: Washburne, Alex
sources.title: Zoonotic Origin Evidence We Don't Have
sources.summary: Washburne Substack cataloging zoonotic-origin evidence that is still missing—intermediate hosts, early animal positives, market chain—versus what lab-leak critics demand.

sources.author: Zhan, Shing Hei, et al.
sources.title: SARS-CoV-2 is well adapted for humans. What does this mean for re-emergence?
sources.summary: Early bioRxiv preprint arguing SARS-CoV-2 appears well adapted to humans from the outset—flagged later in classified analyses for FCS/adaptation implications (chapter notes).

sources.author: Fauci, Anthony S.
sources.title: Research on Highly Pathogenic H5N1 Influenza Virus: The Way Forward
sources.summary: Fauci’s 2012 mBio commentary defending a path forward for highly pathogenic H5N1 research amid gain-of-function controversy.
sources.book_role: Fauci’s own earlier writing that a GoF experiment gone wrong could start a pandemic.

sources.author: Klotz, Lynn
sources.title: Human error in high-biocontainment labs: a likely pandemic threat
sources.summary: Pre-COVID Bulletin warning that human error in high-biocontainment labs is a likely pandemic threat—lab-accident risk as mainstream biosafety concern.

sources.title: Competitive Consultation on Central Air Conditioning Renovation Project of the Wuhan Institute of Virology
sources.publication: China Government Procurement Network, Chinese Academy of Sciences
sources.summary: Archived Sept 2019 procurement notice for WIV central air-conditioning renovation—cited in debates over pre-outbreak lab infrastructure problems. Thin archive capture.

sources.author: Dilanian, Ken, et al.
sources.title: Report says cellphone data suggests October shutdown at Wuhan lab, but experts are skeptical
sources.summary: NBC/Yahoo report on a disputed claim that cellphone data showed an October 2019 Wuhan-lab shutdown—experts skeptical.

sources.author: Allen, Nick
sources.title: US and UK intelligence agencies 'examining report on mobile phone data at Wuhan laboratory'
sources.summary: Archived Telegraph report that U.S. and UK intelligence were examining the mobile-phone data claims about the Wuhan laboratory.

sources.author: Ai, Hongxia
sources.title: Dedicated airport port-of-entry for the Military World Games opened for testing
sources.summary: Xinhua (archived) on opening a dedicated airport port-of-entry for the Wuhan Military World Games testing—pre-outbreak mass international military gathering in Wuhan.

sources.author: Quay, Steven Carl
sources.title: Where Did the 2019 Coronavirus Pandemic Begin and How Did it Spread? The People's Liberation Army Hospital in Wuhan China and Line 2 of the Wuhan Metro System Are Compelling Answers
sources.summary: Quay Zenodo preprint arguing PLA hospital and Wuhan Metro Line 2 as compelling early-spread nodes—alternative geography of the outbreak’s start.

notes_sources.author: Chen, Nanshan et al.
notes_sources.title: Epidemiological and clinical characteristics of 99 cases of 2019 novel coronavirus pneumonia in Wuhan, China: a descriptive study
notes_sources.summary: Lancet descriptive study of 99 early 2019 novel coronavirus pneumonia cases in Wuhan—epidemiological and clinical characteristics from the first hospital series. Page body not captured (ad/shell only).
notes_sources.book_role: Notes citation for one of the first peer-reviewed Wuhan clinical case series.

notes_sources.author: Li, Qun, et al.
notes_sources.title: Early Transmission Dynamics in Wuhan, China, of Novel Coronavirus–Infected Pneumonia
notes_sources.publication: The New England Journal of Medicine
notes_sources.summary: NEJM analysis by Li et al. of early Wuhan transmission dynamics among the first 425 confirmed cases—mean incubation ~5.2 days, early doubling every ~7.4 days, and a sharp drop in Huanan market linkage after January 1, 2020.
notes_sources.book_role: Notes citation quantifying early human-to-human spread beyond the market cluster.

orgs: The New England Journal of Medicine

notes_sources.author: Kumar, Sudhir, et al.
notes_sources.title: An Evolutionary Portrait of the Progenitor SARS-CoV-2 and Its Dominant Offshoots in COVID-19 Pandemic
notes_sources.summary: Molecular Biology and Evolution paper reconstructing SARS-CoV-2’s likely most recent common ancestor and dominant early lineages from thousands of genomes—mapping cryptic mutational history and spatiotemporal spread.
notes_sources.book_role: Notes citation reconstructing progenitor SARS-CoV-2 and early lineage offshoots.

notes_sources.author: Helden, Jacques van, et al.
notes_sources.title: An appeal for an objective, open, and transparent scientific debate about the origin of SARS-CoV-2
notes_sources.summary: Lancet correspondence led by Jacques van Helden and dozens of scientists appealing for an open, transparent origins debate—arguing a research-related origin remains plausible and must not be excluded a priori.
notes_sources.book_role: Notes citation for the open scientific appeal to keep lab origin on the table.

notes_sources.author: Markson, Sharri
notes_sources.title: What Really Happened In Wuhan: A Virus Like No Other, Countless Infections, Millions of Deaths
notes_sources.summary: Sharri Markson’s 2021 book What Really Happened In Wuhan, investigating early outbreak timeline, infections, and origins claims. Amazon product page only; no book text captured.
notes_sources.book_role: Notes citation for Markson’s book-length Wuhan origins investigation.

notes_sources.author: Eban, Katherine, and Jeff Kao
notes_sources.title: COVID-19 Origins: Investigating a “Complex and Grave Situation” Inside a Wuhan Lab
notes_sources.summary: Vanity Fair/ProPublica investigation with Senate analyst Toy Reid decoding WIV ‘party speak’ archives—highlighting a November 2019 ‘complex and grave situation’ and biosafety concerns used to bolster lab-linked origins scrutiny.
notes_sources.book_role: Notes citation on WIV internal documents and the Nov 2019 crisis language.

notes_sources.author: Demaneuf, Gilles
notes_sources.title: Translations of key Chinese articles and blogs about the Covid-19 Outbreak
notes_sources.summary: Gilles Demaneuf Medium compilation of English translations of key Chinese articles and blogs on the early COVID outbreak—preserving pieces often later deleted from Chinese media.
notes_sources.book_role: Notes citation preserving translated Chinese primary reporting on the outbreak’s start.

notes_sources.author: Kopp, Emily
notes_sources.title: ‘The CT machines were crashing’: Interview with Wuhan doctor reveals early COVID cases were suppressed
notes_sources.summary: USRTK report on a Caixin interview with a Wuhan radiologist who saw CT-confirmed cases doubling daily in January 2020 while official counts froze—estimating ≥10,000 city cases by Jan 21 amid pressure not to speak publicly.
notes_sources.book_role: Notes citation for firsthand evidence that early Wuhan case counts were suppressed.

notes_sources.author: Deslandes, Alexandre, et al.
notes_sources.title: SARS-CoV-2 was already spreading in France in late December 2019
notes_sources.summary: PubMed abstract of Deslandes et al.: retrospective RT-PCR on a late-December 2019 Paris ICU patient with unexplained haemoptysis—evidence consistent with SARS-CoV-2 circulating in France before the recognized January 2020 start.
notes_sources.book_role: Notes citation for a purported pre-recognition European clinical COVID case.

notes_sources.title: First detection of SARS-CoV-2 in untreated wastewaters in Italy
notes_sources.summary: PubMed abstract of La Rosa et al.: first detection of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in untreated Italian wastewaters—demonstrating wastewater-based epidemiology as an early community circulation signal.
notes_sources.book_role: Notes citation for early European wastewater detection of SARS-CoV-2.

notes_sources.author: Fongaro, Gislaine, et al.
notes_sources.title: The presence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in human sewage in Santa Catarina, Brazil, November 2019
notes_sources.summary: Science of the Total Environment study detecting SARS-CoV-2 RNA in Santa Catarina, Brazil sewage as early as November 2019—pushing putative circulation in the Americas before official first cases.
notes_sources.book_role: Notes citation for Brazilian wastewater evidence of late-2019 SARS-CoV-2 RNA.

notes_sources.author: Young, Alison
notes_sources.title: Could an accident have caused COVID-19? Why the Wuhan lab-leak theory shouldn't be dismissed
notes_sources.summary: Alison Young USA Today opinion arguing the Wuhan lab-leak hypothesis should not be dismissed—drawing on her lab-safety investigations (including forgotten NIH smallpox vials) to show high-containment accidents and lapses are real precedents.
notes_sources.book_role: Notes citation that mainstream reporting urged taking lab accident seriously.

notes_sources.author: Young, Alison
notes_sources.title: Pandora’s Gamble: Lab Leaks, Pandemics, and a World at Risk
notes_sources.summary: Alison Young’s 2023 book Pandora’s Gamble on lab leaks, pandemics, and biosafety risk—extending her investigative reporting on high-containment accidents. Amazon page only; no book text captured.
notes_sources.book_role: Notes citation for Young’s book-length treatment of lab-leak risk.
